Subject: Novagraphics pilot — request for commercial exception (escrow credit)

Team — looping you in on a commercial exception request from Novagraphics (prospect -> strategic pilot). Key ask from the customer: 50% credit on first three months of consumption as an escrowed credit to offset their onboarding risk. High-level:

- Prospect: Novagraphics (health analytics)
- Ask: 50% MOP credit applied as escrow, released monthly based on usage milestones (see attached workbook)
- Commitment: 18 months; pilot months count toward tiering
- Commercial rationale: large potential ARR ($1.1M TCV) and strategic logos in the health vertical; fast-start required to get clinical integration underway

Attachments: novagraphics_mop_pricing.xlsx (MOP model + proposed credit schedule)

Need: VP/CFO sign-off for an exception to standard make-good limits and to approve escrow mechanism. Can we get quick guidance on whether we should:

1) Approve as-requested (50% x 3 months in escrow)
2) Counter with a staged credit (e.g., 30% month 1, 20% month 2, 10% month 3) tied to usage triggers
3) Require a make-good cap and legal-approved escrow agreement

Customer urgency: they want commercial terms by EOD Thursday to hit a developer onboarding window the following week.

Sana — wanted to be transparent about internal approvals; I flagged the ask as an exception vs our standard onboarding credit.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novagraphics pilot — request for commercial exception (escrow credit)

Marissa — thanks for the note and the workbook. Quick thoughts from a GTM/GM POV:

- The TCV math looks attractive but the requested structure (+50% escrow up front) materially impacts near-term margin and defeats our normal ramp protections.
- Preference: a milestone-tied staggered credit preserves alignment. Suggested counter: 30% month 1, 15% month 2, 5% month 3 (released on incremental usage thresholds) + a one-time onboarding professional services credit capped at $15k.
- If the customer insists on escrow accounting, require RevOps to hold funds in escrow with explicit release triggers; legal to finalize escrow language.

I'll be blunt: approving the full 50% upfront sets a precedent. If we approve, we should ensure a) a firm TCV commitment (signed SOW), and b) a make-good clause with clawback for low usage.

Cc'ing Markus for visibility on any finance tolerances we should be prepared to accept.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Enterprise Accounts
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novagraphics pilot — request for commercial exception (escrow credit)

Marissa / Karthik — I ran a quick packet-level analysis and filled out the commercial exception form (attached). Highlights:

- Estimated ARR (post-pilot conversion): ~$1.1M, first-year recognized revenue ~ $420k (conservative adoption)
- Gross margin impact of requested 50% escrow = ~8.7 percentage points in year 1 if released as requested
- Recommended guardrails:
  * Approve a staged escrow release tied to monthly consumption milestones (30/15/5)
  * One-time onboarding services credit to be applied against professional services line, not against compute consumption
  * Make-good/clawback for <30% of projected usage in first 90 days
  * Cap total commercial concession at $75,000

Attachments: commercial_exception_form.pdf

Recommendation: Approve conditional exception with the above guardrails. If Sales wants the full 50% up front, we need explicit CFO sign-off and a documented precedent note for Finance.

Kimberly Park
Director, RevOps & Finance Partnerships
kimberly_park@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Novagraphics pilot — request for commercial exception (escrow credit)

FYI — drafting an executive memo below that we can present to Finance/CFO for sign-off. Please edit in-line if you want different language; I will forward to Markus once we land wording.

--- Exec memo (for CFO review) ---
Request: Approve commercial exception for Novagraphics pilot to allow an escrowed onboarding credit.

Rationale:
- Strategic value: Novagraphics is a high-profile prospect in the health analytics vertical with expected TCV ~$1.1M. Fast onboarding accelerates clinical integration and reference potential.
- Risk: Customer requests 50% credit on first three months as escrow; release tied to usage. This creates near-term margin pressure and a precedent risk.

Proposed decision (preferred): Approve a conditional exception with the following terms:
- Credit schedule: 30% month 1, 15% month 2, 5% month 3 (released on monthly usage thresholds detailed in attached workbook)
- Make-good/clawback: full clawback for <30% of projected usage in first 90 days; pro-rata clawback for partial attainment
- Cap: $75,000 maximum commercial concession
- Legal: require escrow agreement and SOW signed before credit release
- Owner: SalesOps to manage release schedule; RevOps to monitor usage and trigger clawback; Legal to execute escrow doc

Time sensitivity: Customer requests terms by EOD Thursday to start integration next week.

Requested action: Aditya/Markus — please confirm approval route (VP-level ok? need CFO signature?) and any edits to the cap or release mechanics. If approved, I will coordinate an exec-signed exception memo and notify the customer.

Marissa
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
